hints: Apply conservation of linear momentum to find the common velocity $v$ after the two particles coalesce: $m_P u_P + m_Q u_Q = (m_P + m_Q)v$.
Calculate the total kinetic energy before the collision: $KE_i = \frac{1}{2}m_P u_P^2 + \frac{1}{2}m_Q u_Q^2$.
Calculate the final combined kinetic energy $KE_f = \frac{1}{2}(m_P + m_Q)v^2$ and subtract it from $KE_i$ to find the loss.
walkthrough:
Apply conservation of linear momentum with $m_P = 0.2\text{ kg}$, $u_P = 5\text{ m s}^{-1}$, $m_Q = 0.1\text{ kg}$, and $u_Q = 2\text{ m s}^{-1}$:
$$0.2(5) + 0.1(2) = (0.2 + 0.1)v$$
$$1.0 + 0.2 = 0.3v \implies 1.2 = 0.3v \implies v = 4\text{ m s}^{-1}$$

Calculate the total kinetic energy before the collision:
$$KE_i = \frac{1}{2}(0.2)(5^2) + \frac{1}{2}(0.1)(2^2) = 0.1(25) + 0.05(4) = 2.5 + 0.2 = 2.7\text{ J}$$

Calculate the total kinetic energy after coalescence:
$$KE_f = \frac{1}{2}(0.2 + 0.1)(4^2) = \frac{1}{2}(0.3)(16) = 2.4\text{ J}$$

Find the kinetic energy lost in the collision:
$$\Delta KE = KE_i - KE_f = 2.7 - 2.4 = 0.3\text{ J}$$
teacher_walkthrough:
Step 1: Common velocity after coalescence.
Because the horizontal plane is smooth, no external horizontal forces act on the system during the collision, so total linear momentum is conserved.
Since both particles move in the same direction, assign this direction as positive:
$$m_P u_P + m_Q u_Q = (m_P + m_Q)v$$
$$0.2(5) + 0.1(2) = (0.2 + 0.1)v$$
$$1.0 + 0.2 = 0.3v$$
$$1.2 = 0.3v$$
$$v = \frac{1.2}{0.3} = 4\text{ m s}^{-1}$$

Step 3: Calculate final kinetic energy ($KE_f$):
After coalescence, the combined mass is $0.2 + 0.1 = 0.3\text{ kg}$ moving at $4\text{ m s}^{-1}$:
$$KE_f = \frac{1}{2}(m_P + m_Q)v^2 = \frac{1}{2}(0.3)(4^2) = 0.15 \times 16 = 2.4\text{ J}$$

Step 4: Determine the kinetic energy lost:
$$\text{Loss} = KE_i - KE_f = 2.7 - 2.4 = 0.3\text{ J}$$
